It does not hold the master key, sessions, invite or reset links or pending join tokens, and every secret in it is sealed under a key that is only inside the encrypted file. The passphrase is sent in the body, is never stored or logged, and is not in the audit entry. 422 passphrase_too_short for fewer than 16 characters; 409 audit_chain_broken when the audit log does not verify; 409 backup_busy while another backup is being prepared. Audited as backup.exported. Needs backup.manage.

post.description: Replaces everything in this Bayplan with the uploaded backup. The backup is opened, migrated to this version, re-keyed to this instance's master key and verified on a private copy first; nothing live changes until all of that has worked. Then Bayplan saves the current database as backups/prerestore-<time>.db, swaps the restored one in and restarts itself. The answer is 202 and Bayplan is unreachable for a moment; everyone is signed out, including the caller. confirm must be this instance's name (422 confirm_mismatch). The same refusals as the check apply and leave everything as it was, and 429 rate_limited when the caller has used their attempts. Audited in the restored log as audit.reanchored then backup.restored; a refused restore is recorded in this log as backup.failed (stage restore_apply) with a reason. Needs backup.manage.

post.description: Does one action to up to 25 containers, each named by its node ID and container ID, and answers one result per target in request order. The actions are start, stop, restart, kill, pause and unpause. A stop or restart uses the container's own stop timeout and signal and a kill sends SIGKILL; a request with exactly one target may set timeout or signal, and a request with more is refused 422 options_single_only. Starting a running container or stopping a stopped one is answered done, and a container removed meanwhile is not_found, so repeating an action is safe. A target is routed by node ID, never by display name. A target that fails never stops the others, and nothing is retried. At most 4 calls run at once on one node and 16 targets at once overall. With more than one target (or a bulkId sent) every audit row of the request carries the same bulk detail, a UUIDv7 the server makes when the client sends none, and the response returns it. Bayplan's own server container and any agent container are protected: to stop, kill, restart or pause one, send a single-target request whose confirm is the container's name (else 422 confirmation_required, and nothing is sent); in a request with more than one target such a container is skipped with code own_container and never acted on. Start and unpause need no confirm. An action on one of them is audited before the call (stage initiated) and after it (stage completed), and a connection that drops during the call is answered done with code connection_lost and audited as stage connection_lost with result success. A node whose agent runs read-only (BAYPLAN_AGENT_READ_ONLY) is refused with host_read_only before any call; an agent that refuses by its own policy, such as one older than the server, is agent_policy_denied. Each target is audited as container.started, container.stopped, container.restarted, container.killed, container.paused or container.unpaused, with result failure and the code when it failed. Needs containers.control (Operator) on the environment.
post.summary: Start, stop, restart, kill, pause or unpause containers

post.description: Removes up to 25 containers, each named by its node ID and container ID, and answers one result per target in request order, as the actions route does. A running container is refused with container_running unless force is true, and nothing is sent for it. Named volumes are never removed. removeVolumes also removes the container's anonymous volumes, and needs the delete volumes permission on top of containers.remove: a caller without it is refused 403 before any call and the refusal is audited as permission.denied. Bayplan's own server container and any agent container are protected: to remove one, send a single-target request whose confirm is the container's name (else 422 confirmation_required, and nothing is sent); in a request with more than one target such a container is skipped with code own_container and never acted on. Start and unpause need no confirm. An action on one of them is audited before the call (stage initiated) and after it (stage completed), and a connection that drops during the call is answered done with code connection_lost and audited as stage connection_lost with result success. Each target is audited as container.removed with its force and volumes choices. Needs containers.remove (Operator) on the environment.

The container lives on one node, named by nodeId (the nodeId of its row in the containers list); it may be left out on an environment of one node and is required on a swarm (422 node_required). The values of the environment variables and of the log driver's options can be credentials: they are withheld on the server, and sent only to a caller who holds secrets.reveal on the environment. env and logConfig.options then list the names with masked true and no value, and masked at the top says something was withheld. The command and the entrypoint can carry credentials too (a password on the command line): without secrets.reveal each is the single entry <hidden> and commandMasked is true. 404 container_not_found when the engine has no such container (it may have been removed meanwhile); 503 node_unavailable when the node is not a connected node of the environment. Needs containers.read (Viewer) on the environment.

get.description: Up to tail lines of the container's log that were written before until, oldest first, for "Load earlier lines". The container lives on one node, named by nodeId, with the same rules and problems as the container detail route (422 node_required, 404 container_not_found, 503 node_unavailable). sid is the viewer's ID, the one its live stream uses: a viewer is audited once however many pages it reads. post.description: Starts an interactive TTY process in a running container and returns a pending session the browser attaches to over a WebSocket within 30 seconds, at wsPath. The session is single use and bound to the caller and the caller's sign-in; the upgrade is accepted only from the instance's public origin. The container lives on one node, named by nodeId, with the same rules and problems as the container detail route (422 node_required, 404 container_not_found, 503 node_unavailable). 422 invalid_shell when a custom command cannot be read. Refused before any exec is made: 429 shell_limit_reached when the caller already holds as many shells as the instance allows (the limit is the errors entry located at limit), 409 host_read_only on a read-only host, 409 own_container for Bayplan's own server or an agent's container (decided from a fresh inspect), 409 container_not_running, 502 agent_policy_denied when the node's agent is too old to run an exec, 409 no_shell when the engine cannot find the command, 503 stream_busy when the host's agent serves as many logs and shells as it can. What is typed and printed is never recorded: the start is audited as shell.opened and the end as shell.closed. Needs containers.exec on the environment (an extra permission: Operator only when granted; Admin always).

The reference is normalised first: nginx:1.27 becomes docker.io/library/nginx:1.27 and no tag means latest. An unparsable reference is 422 ref_invalid and starts nothing. At most 5 pulls of one user run at once (429 too_many_pulls). Each node pulls once, is never retried, and writes one image.pulled audit row. Needs images.pull (Operator) on the environment.

post.description: Removes up to 25 image copies, each named by its node ID and image ID, and answers one result per target in request order. An image with several names has each name untagged first and is then deleted by ID, so the engine's must-be-forced refusal never stops a removal; force is never sent. An image that any container on its node, running or stopped, references is never removed there, and an image that any swarm service spec references, even with no task, is never removed on any node, because Swarm would pull it again: the result is failed with code image_in_use and the detail names up to 5 users. The containers are read again from the node just before each removal and the service specs from a manager, and a container that starts between the check and the call makes the engine refuse and is answered image_in_use too. On a swarm whose services cannot be read nothing is removed and the target is node_unreachable. An image the node does not have is failed with code not_found and writes no audit row. One that fails never stops the others. A request that names more than one image, or sends a bulkId, is a bulk delete of dangling images: a target whose image has a name is skipped with code not_dangling, nothing is sent for it and it writes no audit row, whatever the browser sent. One image, on one or several nodes, is removed whatever its names. Needs images.delete (Operator) on the environment. With more than one target (or a bulkId sent) every audit row of the request carries the same bulk detail, a UUIDv7 the server makes when the client sends none, and the response returns it. Every attempt on an image the node has is audited as image.removed, failures included.

post.description: Deletes up to 25 volumes, each named by its node ID and name, and answers one result per target in request order. This is irreversible: the data in the volume is gone. The caller types the confirmation: the volume's name for a single target, or delete {n} volumes for several, where n is at least the number of targets in the request (else 422 confirmation_required and nothing is sent). Volumes are node-local: a volume is deleted on the node named, and the same name on another node is left alone. A volume that any container on its node, running or stopped, or any swarm service mounts is never deleted: the result is failed with code volume_in_use and the detail names up to 5 users. The users are read again from the node and from a manager just before each removal, and force is never sent, so a container that mounts the volume between the check and the call makes the engine refuse and is answered volume_in_use too. A volume the node does not have is failed with code not_found. One that fails never stops the others. Needs volumes.delete (an Operator or above with the delete volumes permission) on the environment; a caller without it is refused 403 and the refusal is audited as permission.denied. With more than one target (or a bulkId sent) every audit row of the request carries the same bulk detail, a UUIDv7 the server makes when the client sends none, and the response returns it. Every attempt on a volume that exists is audited as volume.removed, failures included.

Needs a Docker socket that answers. 409 socket_not_found, engine_unreachable, unsupported_engine (unless allowUnsupported) or local_environment_exists. kind agent creates an environment for hosts that run the Bayplan agent, with its own certificate authority and a join token, and answers install with the token (shown once) and the swarm and standalone install commands and files, built from the address agents dial (the agent URL, else the public URL, with its base path); 409 public_url_required when Bayplan has neither, and 409 insecure_agent_url when that address is plain ws:// for a host that is not this machine and BAYPLAN_AGENT_ALLOW_INSECURE is off. Nothing is created in either case. 422 invalid_name. The name defaults to the hostname the daemon, or the first agent, reports. Needs environments.create. Audited as environment.added.
post.summary: Add an environment

get.description: After a restore from a backup, agents that were installed after the backup was taken present a certificate the environment issued but are not in the restored database, and are refused unknown_agent. This lists the ones that tried in the last 24 hours, newest first, from memory: it is empty after a restart until they try again, and an agent drops off 24 hours after it stops trying. Each is reinstalled with its environment's install command. Needs environments.token (instance admin).
get.summary: List the agents Bayplan does not know

get.description: Derived from live state, never stored, so an item is there exactly while its cause is and cannot be dismissed: an environment that is offline (env_offline, with since and reason), a certificate that is not renewing or has expired (cert_not_renewing), agents that need an update by hand (manual_update_needed, one item with a count), a clock that is out of step (clock_skew), an environment still waiting for its first agent after 7 days (pending_long), a swarm that was re-initialised (cluster_changed) and a local host that can be folded into a swarm environment it manages (fold_offered, only for callers who hold environments.manage). Only environments the caller holds environments.read for are considered, so the list never reveals what the caller cannot open, and the counts are over that set. A revoked environment says nothing here. Errors come first, then the newest. Names are at most 64 characters.
get.summary: List the environment problems that need attention

delete.description: Needs environments.delete. Stops managing the host. Revokes every agent, disables the join token and deletes the environment, and changes nothing in Docker: its containers, networks and volumes are untouched (D-20, D-30). With uninstallAgents=true each online agent is first told to uninstall itself (a swarm's agents through one manager, which removes the agent service and its token secret; every agent removes its own container and state volume), and the request waits up to 30 seconds for their answers. Whatever they answer, or do not, the revoking and deletion follow, so hosts that were offline or refused keep their agent until the admin runs the manual cleanup command that GET /api/env/{envId}/agents gives. Audited as environment.removed, agent.revoked per agent, and agent.uninstalled per agent that confirmed.

parameters.description: Also tell every online agent of the environment to remove itself from its host before the environment is removed

schema.description: Also tell every online agent of the environment to remove itself from its host before the environment is removed

post.description: Offered when the Docker host Bayplan runs on is a manager of a swarm that is enrolled through agents: the local socket's own /info must report the cluster ID that the swarm environment is bound to (foldOffered is true on both environments). The swarm environment then reaches that node through the Docker socket and expects no agent on it, the node counts once however it is reached, and the separate local socket environment is retired, in one transaction. Nothing changes on the host or in Docker. Answers the swarm environment. 404 environment_not_found; 409 fold_not_offered when the host is not a manager of that swarm, or was folded already. Needs environments.manage. Audited as environment.local_folded.
post.summary: Fold this Bayplan host into a swarm environment

delete.description: The current join token enrols nobody from now on. Agents that are already enrolled keep working. Rotating the token makes a new one and enables enrolment again. Disabling a disabled token changes nothing. 404 environment_not_found. Needs environments.token. Audited as environment.token_disabled.

get.description: The generation, when and by whom it was made, and whether it is disabled. Never the token: it is stored only as a hash. 404 environment_not_found. Needs environments.token.

post.description: Makes a new join token and retires the current one in the same transaction. The old install command stops enrolling hosts at once; agents that are already enrolled keep their certificates and are not disconnected. Answers the install object for the new token, once, with Cache-Control no-store; when the environment is a swarm that already has agents it carries the one-line rotate command. 404 environment_not_found; 409 public_url_required when Bayplan has no address to give agents, and 409 insecure_agent_url when that address is plain ws:// for a host that is not this machine and BAYPLAN_AGENT_ALLOW_INSECURE is off; the current token stays in both cases. Needs environments.token. Audited as environment.token_rotated with the new generation.
post.summary: Rotate an environment's join token

get.description: The pull as it stands now, for a browser that returns to a pull it started. A pull is kept for 10 minutes after it ends. Only the user who started it, or an instance admin, can read it; anyone else gets 404 pull_not_found.
get.summary: One pull job and its progress on every node

post.description: Stops the nodes that have not finished: their downloads are cancelled, their items end cancelled and write an image.pulled audit row with the code cancelled. A cancel by someone other than the user who started the pull also writes an image.pull_cancelled row, with the canceller as the actor and the starter named. Nodes that had finished keep the image and stay done. The job ends cancelled when no node finished and partial otherwise, and the answer is the job as it stands, normally already ended. Only the user who started the pull, or a holder of images.pull on the pull's environment, may cancel it: anyone else who may not see the pull gets 404 pull_not_found, and one who sees it but cannot cancel gets 403 (audited as permission.denied). A pull that has already ended answers 409 pull_finished and nothing changes, so cancelling twice is safe. A cancel is a change and is never retried.
post.summary: Cancel a pull that is running

get.description: An instance admin sees every credential. Anyone who holds images.read on at least one environment sees the instance credentials, and an environment's own credentials when they can read that environment; canManage says whether they may change a credential. A caller with no images.read anywhere gets an empty list. No secret is ever included.
get.summary: List the registry credentials the signed-in user may see

post.description: Stores a sign-in for a registry host and an optional namespace, used for pulls and tag browsing on every environment. The secret is sealed with the vault, included in backups and re-wrapped by key rotation, and never returned by any route afterwards: the answer carries only its last 4 characters, and only for a secret of 12 or more characters. Needs registries.instance, which only instance admins hold. 422 validation_failed names every field at fault with a stable code (name_required, name_invalid, type_invalid, host_required, host_invalid, prefix_invalid, username_required, secret_required, hub_prefix_required, hub_fallback_not_hub, expiry_invalid, expiry_past, ca_invalid); 409 credential_name_taken, host_prefix_taken or hub_fallback_taken when another instance credential clashes; the 409 names that credential in its errors list (location conflict.credential). Audited as registry.credential_created without the secret.
post.summary: Add an instance registry credential

get.description: Derived from live state, never stored, so an item is there exactly while its cause is: a credential that expires within 7 days (expiring), whose expiry day has passed (expired) or that its registry refused on the last use and that has not worked since (auth_failed). An expiry day counts as the end of that day in UTC, and the 7-day warning and expired use that same instant. Only credentials the caller may manage are listed: an instance admin gets instance and environment credentials, an Env Admin the credentials of the environments they administer, and everyone else an empty list. A credential with several problems has one item, the most severe. Nothing is renewed automatically.
get.summary: List the registry credentials that need attention

get.description: Lists a repository's tag names through the server, with the stored credential pulls would use for it among the ones the caller may see: the instance credentials and, with envId, that environment's own. The tags come newest version first and then by name, descending, 100 to a page (page, from 0), filtered by the text q and without signature, attestation and cache tags unless hide is false. The answer names the credential, never holds it, and is cached for a minute per credential, so a caller never gets a list fetched with a credential they cannot use. Needs images.read on at least one environment, and on envId when it is given (403). An unparsable reference is 422 ref_invalid. At most 60 tag requests a minute per user (a burst of 30), lists and details together: 429 rate_limited. When the registry cannot list the tags the answer is 404 repository_not_found or repository_unavailable (the registry refused the repository although the credential's sign-in works, so it does not exist or the account cannot read it), or 502 with the problem type needs_login (the registry wants a login and no stored credential matches), login_refused (it refused the matching credential), registry_unreachable or registry_tls; errors names the registry as registry.host and registry.repo and the credential used, if any, as credential.id, credential.name, credential.scopeKind and credential.scopeName. Not audited.

post.description: Reads the digest, the created date and the platforms of up to 25 tags of a repository, for the rows the person can see. The server asks the registry with the same credential and the same authorisation as the tag list: images.read on at least one environment, and on envId when it is given (403, audited), an unparsable reference is 422 ref_invalid, the limit of the tag list applies (429 rate_limited), 26 tags are 422 and so is a tag that is not 1 to 128 letters, digits, underscores, dots or dashes (tag_invalid). Docker Hub is read through its tags API, which costs no pulls; any other registry through a manifest HEAD and, per digest, the manifest and the config of one platform (linux/amd64, else the environment's node architecture, else the first). Results are cached per credential, repository and digest. A tag that could not be read carries a code, never a failure of the request. Not audited.
post.summary: Read the digest, date and platforms of tags

post.description: Runs the registry's own flow from the Bayplan server in three steps and reports each one: whether the registry answers, whether it accepts the sign-in, and, when a test repository is given, whether the sign-in can read it. Works on values that are not saved. A 401 to the unauthenticated ping counts as reachable; a refused sign-in is reported as refused whether the registry says 401 or 403; a registry that asks for no login reports signed in as not_checked. Each step is a state and a code, never text from the registry. The server refuses link-local, unspecified and multicast addresses (cloud metadata included) after DNS, allows private and loopback ranges, and refuses redirects to plain HTTP or local URLs. Needs registries.instance. At most 10 tests a minute per user across both families: 429 rate_limited. 422 validation_failed names the fields at fault with the codes of adding a credential, ca_invalid and test_repository_invalid. caPem and insecure apply the credential's own CA and switch to this test only; the operator's BAYPLAN_REGISTRY_BLOCK_CIDRS ranges stay refused even with the switch on. A stored credential's secret is lent only to the host, type, username, CA and insecure switch it was stored with: a test that changes any of them needs a secret typed now (422 secret_required). Audited as registry.credential_tested with each step's result, never the secret.
post.summary: Test a registry sign-in from the server

post.description: Asks one node of the environment envId to read the manifest of repository:tag (latest when left out) from the credential's registry with the credential, through its agent and its own engine. A firewall, an internal DNS name or a certificate authority that only the node has shows up here and cannot show up in the server's own test. The engine reads the manifest with a HEAD, which Docker Hub does not count as a pull. On a swarm the check runs on one connected manager, else on the one node; the answer names the node. Works on values that are not saved, or on a stored instance credential (credentialId). The answer is 200 whether the node could pull or not: state is passed or failed, and a failed one carries a code (pull_denied, pull_unauthorized, image_not_found, registry_unreachable, registry_tls, registry_http, rate_limited, pull_failed, agent_policy_denied when the node's agent is older than this server, node_unavailable when the node did not answer), never any text from the registry. Needs registries.instance. 422 repository_required without a repository; 422 validation_failed names the other fields at fault (tag_invalid, test_repository_invalid and those of adding a credential); 404 environment_not_found; 503 node_unavailable when no node of the environment is connected; 502 agent_policy_denied when the environment cannot be read. The 10 tests a minute per user are shared with the server tests: 429 rate_limited. The stored secret is lent only to the host, type, username, CA and insecure switch it was stored with (422 secret_required otherwise). A host that is, or resolves on the server to, an address the server's egress policy refuses (cloud metadata, link-local, BAYPLAN_REGISTRY_BLOCK_CIDRS) is not sent to the node: the answer is failed with registry_unreachable. Audited as registry.credential_tested with the environment, the node and via env, never the secret.
post.summary: Test a registry sign-in from an environment's node

delete.description: Removes the credential and its sealed secret. Pulls it would have matched fall back to the next matching credential, or to anonymous; nothing else refers to it. Needs registries.instance. A credential that is already gone, and one of an environment, answer 404 credential_not_found, so a repeated delete is safe and writes nothing. Audited as registry.credential_deleted without the secret.

get.description: The credential as the list shows it. One the caller may not see answers exactly like one that does not exist: 404 credential_not_found.
get.summary: Read one registry credential

patch.description: Changes the members that are sent and keeps the rest. The secret is write-only: leave it out or send it empty to keep the stored one, which is neither read nor returned; send a new one and it is sealed again and replaces it, and the answer carries only its last 4 characters (12 or more characters). Leaving it out keeps the stored one only while the host, type, username, CA and insecure switch stay as stored: changing any of them needs a secret typed now (422 validation_failed, secret_required on body.secret), so the stored secret never goes to a destination it was not stored for. There is no scope: a credential never moves between layers. Needs registries.instance. A credential of an environment answers 404 credential_not_found here, exactly like one that does not exist. 422 validation_failed names every field at fault with the same codes as adding; 409 credential_name_taken, host_prefix_taken or hub_fallback_taken when another instance credential clashes, naming it in its errors list (location conflict.credential). Audited as registry.credential_updated with a changed detail listing the names of the fields that changed, the secret only as the word secret, and host_from and host_to when the host changed.

get.description: publicUrlLocked is true when the BAYPLAN_PUBLIC_URL environment variable fixes the public URL (D-04), agentUrlLocked when BAYPLAN_AGENT_URL fixes the agent URL (D-18). agentEndpoint is the address agents dial: the agent URL, else the public URL, with its path and /agent/connect. enrolledAgents counts the agents that are not revoked and offlineAgents those of them with no connection now (D-19). agentEndpointRefused is true when agentEndpoint is plain ws:// for a host that is not this machine and BAYPLAN_AGENT_ALLOW_INSECURE is off: agents cannot connect to it (G-02-R4-3).
get.summary: Get the instance name, public URL and agent URL

patch.description: Only the fields sent are changed. Invalid fields answer 422 with a stable code per field (instance_name_required, instance_name_too_long, invalid_public_url, invalid_agent_url, insecure_agent_url). An agent URL that is plain http for a host that is not this machine answers 422 insecure_agent_url unless BAYPLAN_AGENT_ALLOW_INSECURE is on, because agents refuse such an address; a loopback or https agent URL, clearing it, and an http public URL are accepted. A different public URL while BAYPLAN_PUBLIC_URL is set answers 409 public_url_locked, and a different agent URL while BAYPLAN_AGENT_URL is set answers 409 agent_url_locked; both change nothing. An empty agentUrl clears it. A change takes effect at once: the Origin check and the cookie Secure flag use the new public URL from the next request. When the address agents dial changes, every agent connected over a TLS-verified session is sent the new address and the server's pins over its tunnel and dials that address from its next connection; an agent takes only a wss:// address this way. From then on the server accepts agent handshakes only for the new host and port, with no fallback period: an agent that was offline or on plain ws:// at the time is refused auth_rejected until it is reinstalled with the new address or the change is reverted. Each change is audited as settings.updated with the old and new value of every changed field.
patch.summary: Change the instance name, the public URL or the agent URL

get.description: idleMinutes is how long a shell may sit without input or output (5 to 240, default 30) and maxPerUser how many open shells one person may hold across all environments (1 to 50, default 10).
get.summary: Get the browser-shell limits

patch.description: Only the fields sent are changed. A value outside its range answers 422. A change takes effect at once: open shells use the new idle limit at their next check, and the next open uses the new cap. A request that changes nothing answers 200 and is not audited. Each change is audited as settings.updated with the old and new value of every changed field.

A remove_member for a user who is not in the team answers 404 member_not_found.

The answer lists what they lost, worked out inside the same step. Audited as one team.member_removed entry carrying impact_count and impact (first ten items "username: environment before→after" joined by "; ", cut to 512 bytes). A user who is not in the team answers 404 member_not_found and nothing is written.

delete.description: Turns the user into a tombstone and cannot be undone: they are disabled, their password, email and display name are cleared, instance admin is turned off, and their sessions, links, direct access and team memberships are removed in one step. Their username stays reserved, so creating it again answers 409 username_reserved. The automations they own pause as owner deleted, except those listed in the optional reassign body, which go to the user named for each in the same step; a user who could not run one answers 422 owner_not_eligible, one that is not the deleted user's answers 404 automation_not_found, and nothing is deleted. The last active instance admin cannot be deleted: 409 last_instance_admin. A user who is already deleted answers 404 user_not_found.

The username can never be changed and is not accepted. An invalid field answers 422 on body.displayName or body.email. Saving what is already there changes nothing.
patch.summary: Edit a user's display name and email

get.description: The user's effective access: for each environment the user can reach, the highest role any source gives, the union of the extra permissions and every source (instance, all, team, direct), computed by the same evaluator that enforces access. An instance admin holds every environment, so the list is empty and instanceAdmin is true. grants lists the user's own grants, the ones editable on the user page. An unknown user answers 404 user_not_found.
get.summary: What a user may do on each environment, and why

post.description: Ends every session of the user at once and refuses their sign-in. Their grants and team memberships are kept and the automations they own pause. Answers the user as they now are. Disabling a disabled user changes nothing. The last active instance admin cannot be disabled: 409 last_instance_admin.
post.summary: Disable a user

post.description: Lets a disabled user sign in again with the grants and teams they had. Enabling an enabled user changes nothing.
post.summary: Enable a user

put.description: Gives the user Admin, Operator or Viewer on one environment (scope env, with envId) or on all of them (scope all). A user holds at most one grant per scope: saving an existing combination edits it (200, audited as access.updated), a new one is created (201, access.granted). Extras are accepted only on Operator: a Viewer answers 422 viewer_cannot_have_extras, an Admin 422 extras_implied and a permission that is not an extra 422 unknown_extra. With expected set, a grant that has changed answers 409 stale_change. A grant never expires. An unknown user answers 404 user_not_found and an unknown environment 404 environment_not_found.
put.summary: Give a user a role on an environment

delete.description: Removes the grant. The user loses the access it gave on their next request and keeps every other grant, and the automations they own that no longer qualify pause. The answer lists who lost which access, worked out inside the same step. Audited as one access.revoked entry carrying the subject, role, scope, impact_count and impact. A grant that is not the user's answers 404 grant_not_found.

post.description: Works out, with the same evaluator that enforces access, who would lose which environment access if the grant were deleted (op delete) or saved with a lower role (op update, with role and extras). The change is applied inside a transaction that is rolled back, so nothing is written and nothing is audited. A grant that is not the user's answers 404 grant_not_found.
post.summary: Preview what removing or changing a user's grant takes away

post.description: Instance authority belongs to a user, never to a team. Setting what is already set changes nothing. Turning it off for the last active instance admin answers 409 last_instance_admin. Answers the user as they now are.
post.summary: Turn instance admin on or off for a user

post.description: For a user who has not yet set a password. The new link replaces the previous one, which stops working at once, and is valid for BAYPLAN_INVITE_TTL. A user who has already set a password answers 409 not_invited; an unknown or deleted user answers 404 user_not_found.
post.summary: Replace a user's invite link

get.description: The git syncs and webhooks that run with the user's permissions, with the environment each acts on and whether it is active or paused because its owner was disabled, deleted or no longer holds the permission it needs. Empty when they own nothing. An unknown or deleted user answers 404 user_not_found.
get.summary: List the automations a user owns

post.description: Ends every session of the user at once, in the same step that makes the link, and answers a one-time link built like an invite's that lets them choose a new password. It is valid for BAYPLAN_INVITE_TTL (72 hours by default) and replaces any link they held. Bayplan sends no email: the admin hands the link over. A disabled user answers 409 user_disabled; an unknown or deleted user answers 404 user_not_found. Audited as user.password_reset_issued with the number of sessions ended.
post.summary: Issue a password reset link

get.description: For an admin on a user's page. No session is marked current. An unknown or deleted user answers 404 user_not_found.
get.summary: List a user's sessions

post.description: Signs the user out everywhere at once and says how many ended. Nothing is written when they were not signed in anywhere. An unknown or deleted user answers 404 user_not_found. Audited as user.sessions_revoked.
post.summary: End all of a user's sessions

post.description: Clears the lock and the failed sign-in count, audited as auth.unlocked with the caller as actor. A user who is not locked is left alone and nothing is audited. Answers the user as they now are.
post.summary: Unlock a locked user

get.summary: Get the running Bayplan version and source link

get.description: Includes data_not_persisted while the data directory would be lost with the container, and key_backup while the encryption key Bayplan generated into the data directory has not been acknowledged (D-15, D-59). The reverse proxy warnings (the proxy_ ones) are listed while Bayplan has seen that problem in the last hour, one item per kind, naming the newest sighting (D-53). refusal_burst lists, for instance admins only, each user who was refused ten or more times in a minute in the last hour (D-20). backup_failed is listed, for instance admins only, while scheduled backups are on and the newest scheduled run failed; subject is why and since is when the last good backup finished (D-32). unknown_agents is listed, for instance admins only, while agents that were installed after the backup this Bayplan was restored from keep trying; count is how many (D-31). The plain-HTTP warning is the browser's to compute and is not listed.
get.summary: List the instance warnings that need an admin's attention

post.description: Records, once for the whole instance, that the generated encryption key has been backed up, and audits it as warning.acknowledged.
post.summary: Acknowledge the encryption key backup reminder
